questions.question: Which of the following options represents the total income earned by individuals from all the sources before deduction of personal income taxes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gross income**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gross income** represents **the total income earned by individuals from all sources before deduction of personal income taxes**.
 
• It includes wages, salaries, bonuses, rental income, interest earnings, and other sources of revenue.
 
• Gross income is crucial for determining an individual's tax liability and eligibility for various financial programs and services.
 
• It is different from net income, which is the income remaining after all deductions and taxes have been subtracted.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Disposable income** is the amount of money that households have available for spending and saving **after income taxes have been accounted for.**
 
• **Personal income** includes all income received by individuals, including wages, dividends, and interest, **before personal taxes are deducted**.
 
• **National income** is the total value of all goods and services produced by a country over a specific period, usually a year.

questions.question: According to which of the following foreign travellers did Dhruvasena II attend Harsha’s assembly at Prayag (Allahabad)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Hiuen Tsang**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hiuen Tsang**, also known as Xuanzang, was a Chinese Buddhist monk, scholar, traveller, and translator who visited India during the reign of King Harshavardhana.
 
• He came to India in the 7th century (precisely around 630 AD) to acquire Buddhist texts and to study at the ancient university of Nalanda.
 
• Hiuen Tsang's detailed accounts provide valuable insights into the political, social, and religious life of India during this period.
 
• He attended the assembly at Prayag (Allahabad) organized by King Harsha, which was a significant religious gathering attended by scholars, monks, and dignitaries from different parts.
 
• His works, especially the **Si-Yu-Ki** or the **Records of the Western World**, are crucial sources of historical information not only about India but also about other regions in Central Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Aspect
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Prayag Assembly**
 Organized by King Harsha, it was a grand religious gathering that attracted scholars, monks, and dignitaries, showcasing the religious tolerance and patronage of Buddhism.
 
 

 **Nalanda University**
 An ancient center of higher learning in Bihar, India, famous for its Buddhist scholarship but also taught other subjects.
 
 

 **Buddhist Pilgrimage**
 Hiuen Tsang's journey to India was part of a broader tradition of Buddhist monks travelling to gain knowledge and religious texts.
 
 

 **Translation Work**
 After returning to China, Hiuen Tsang dedicated his life to translating the Buddhist scriptures he had collected into Chinese, significantly influencing Chinese Buddhism.
 
 

 **Legacy**
 Hiuen Tsang is remembered for his contributions to the spread of Buddhism and for his detailed accounts that offer insights into medieval Indian history.

questions.question: The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Fourth Amendment) Bill, 2022 was passed in Rajya Sabha in December 2022. It seeks to amend the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, with respect to its application to the State of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Karnataka**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Fourth Amendment) Bill, 2022 aims to amend the **Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950**.
 
• The amendment specifically pertains to its application to the state of **Karnataka**.
 
• The bill was passed in the **Rajya Sabha** in December 2022.
 
• The amendment aims to include certain communities in the list of **Scheduled Tribes** in Karnataka.
 
• This move is intended to provide these communities with the benefits and protections accorded to Scheduled Tribes under the **Indian Constitution**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Scheduled Tribes in India** are specific indigenous communities that are recognized by the Indian Constitution. They are provided with certain benefits and protections to promote social and economic development. These communities are identified in the **Scheduled Tribes list** which is periodically updated by the government.

 
 

 Term
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Scheduled Tribes
 Indigenous communities recognized by the Indian Constitution for special benefits.
 
 

 Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950
 An order that lists the recognized Scheduled Tribes across various states in India.
 
 

 Rajya Sabha
 The upper house of India's Parliament where the bill was passed.
 
 

 Amendment Bill
 A formal change or addition proposed during the process of legislation.
 
 

 Karnataka
 A state in India to which the amendment bill pertains.

questions.question: Based on current scientific knowledge, it is currently postulated that the Earth has an estimated age of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **about 4,50,00,00,000 years**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Scientific consensus** estimates the age of the Earth to be about 4.5 billion years.
 
• This age is determined using **radiometric age dating** of meteorite material and Earth's oldest rocks.
 
• The age of the Earth is consistent with the **age of the solar system**, which is also about 4.5 billion years.
 
• Techniques such as **uranium-lead dating** are commonly used to determine these ages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The age of the Earth is a critical piece of information for understanding the history and formation of our planet. The estimation of Earth's age has evolved over centuries through advancements in scientific techniques and understanding.

 
 

 Method
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Radiometric Dating**
 Uses the decay of radioactive isotopes to date materials and determine the age of rocks and fossils.
 
 

 **Uranium-Lead Dating**
 A radiometric dating method that uses the decay of uranium isotopes into lead to determine the age of a mineral.
 
 

 **Carbon Dating**
 Used to date organic materials by measuring the decay of carbon-14, effective for up to 50,000 years.
 
 

 **Geological Stratigraphy**
 Studies the layers of rock (strata) to understand the sequence of geological events and the relative age of rocks.

questions.question: What kind of energy is associated with falling coconuts, speeding cars, rolling stones and flying aircraft?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Kinetic Energy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kinetic energy** is the energy that an object possesses due to its motion.
 
• It depends on the **mass** of the object and the **square of its velocity**, showing a direct proportionality to both.
 
• The formula for kinetic energy is **KE = 1/2 mv²**, where **m** is mass and **v** is velocity.
 
• Objects like **falling coconuts, speeding cars, rolling stones, and flying aircraft** all have kinetic energy because they are in motion.
 
• Kinetic energy can be **transformed** into other forms of energy, such as potential energy, but cannot be destroyed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Kinetic Energy** plays a crucial role in various physical phenomena and engineering applications:

 
• It is a key factor in the **work-energy principle**, which is used in physics to solve problems related to motion and force.
 
• In **renewable energy technologies**, such as wind turbines, kinetic energy from wind is converted into electrical energy.
 
• In **automobile safety**, understanding kinetic energy helps in designing more effective safety features like airbags and crumple zones, which absorb kinetic energy during a crash.
 
• The concept of kinetic energy is also applied in **sports science** to enhance the performance of athletes by optimizing their motion.
 
• In **astrophysics**, kinetic energy is a key factor in understanding celestial phenomena, such as the impact of meteorites on planets.

__
 
• Bharatmala Pariyojana:

 
 
• It is an umbrella program for the highways sector envisaged by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. Hence, Option 1 is correct.
 
• Under Phase-I of Bharatmala Pariyojana, implementation of 34,800 km of national highways in 5 years (from 2017 to 2022) has been approved at an estimated outlay of Rs. 5,35,000 crore.
 
• National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has mandated the development of about 27,500 km of national highways under Phase-I.
 
• However, as per ICRA Limited, Phase-I is likely to be delayed by four years due to the prevailing uncertainty due to Covid-19 and the consequent impact on valuations.

• Phase-II envisages around 48,000 km of road network across India by 2024.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Objectives of Bharatmala Pariyojana:

 
 
• To optimize the efficiency of freight and passenger movement across the country by bridging critical infrastructure gaps through effective interventions.
 
• The effective interventions include the development of economic corridors, inter corridors and feeder routes, national corridor efficiency improvement, border, and international connectivity roads, coastal and port connectivity roads, and greenfield expressways.
 
• Economic Corridors: These are integrated networks of infrastructure within a geographical area designed to stimulate economic development.
 
• Greenfield Projects: They lack constraints imposed by prior work on the site. Typically, it entails development on a completely vacant site and architects start completely from scratch.
 
• Brownfield Projects: They carry constraints related to the current state of the site and might be contaminated or have existing structures that architects have to tear down or modify in some way before the project can move forward.
 
• To generate a large number of direct and indirect employment opportunities in the construction and infrastructure sector and also as part of the enhanced economic activity resulting from better road connectivity across the country.
 
• To connect 550 districts in the country through national highway linkages.

questions.question: Which Committee had suggested a penalty or punishment for the non-performance of Fundamental Duties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Swaran Singh Committee**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Swaran Singh Committee** was constituted by the Government of India in 1976.
 
• It was formed to study the Constitution of India and suggest amendments.
 
• One of the notable recommendations was the inclusion of a list of **Fundamental Duties** for the citizens of India.
 
• The committee suggested that there should be a penalty or punishment for the non-performance of these duties.
 
• Based on its recommendations, the **42nd Amendment Act** of 1976 was enacted, which added the Fundamental Duties to the Constitution under Article 51A.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Amendment
 Description
 
 
 
 

 42nd Amendment Act, 1976
 Known as the **"Mini-Constitution"**, it made significant changes to the Constitution, including the addition of Fundamental Duties.
 
 

 Article 51A
 Specifies the **Fundamental Duties** of the citizens of India, encouraging respect for the Constitution, national symbols, and promoting harmony.
 
 

 Penalty for Non-Performance
 Although suggested by the Swaran Singh Committee, no direct penalty or punishment was incorporated for non-performance of Fundamental Duties.
 
 

 Constitutional Amendments
 The introduction of Fundamental Duties was part of broader efforts to amend the Constitution to address emerging challenges and strengthen the nation's fabric.
 
 

 Current Scenario
 As of now, Fundamental Duties are considered moral obligations for all citizens but are not enforceable by law.

• **Abdul Hamid Lahori** was a court historian during the reign of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan.
 
• He is best known for writing the **'Badshah Nama'**, an official history of Shah Jahan's reign.
 
• The **'Badshah Nama'** is written in Persian and is considered an important source of information about the Mughal Empire.
 
• It provides detailed accounts of Shah Jahan's administration, military campaigns, and architectural projects, including the construction of the Taj Mahal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Term
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Badshah Nama**
 A historical account of the reign of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan, written by Abdul Hamid Lahori.
 
 

 **Shah Jahan**
 The fifth Mughal Emperor, known for commissioning the Taj Mahal.
 
 

 **Mughal Empire**
 A major empire in Indian history, known for its rich cultural and architectural achievements.
 
 

 **Persian Language**
 The language in which the 'Badshah Nama' was written; it was the official language of the Mughal court.
 
 

 **Historian**
 An expert in or student of history, especially that of a particular period, geographical region, or social phenomenon.

questions.question: What will be the average kinetic energy per molecule in SI units for an ideal gas at a temperature of 25°C?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **6.17 × 10^-21 J**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Temperature Conversion:** The temperature of 25ºC needs to be converted to Kelvin, which is 25 + 273.15 = 298.15 K.
 
• **Formula:** The average kinetic energy per molecule in an ideal gas is given by (3/2)kT, where k is the Boltzmann constant (1.38 × 10^-23 J/K).
 
• **Calculation:** Substituting the values, KE = (3/2) × 1.38 × 10^-23 J/K × 298.15 K.
 
• **Result:** After performing the multiplication, KE ≈ 6.17 × 10^-21 J.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Ideal Gas:** An ideal gas is a theoretical gas composed of many randomly moving point particles that interact only through elastic collisions.

 
 

 Parameter
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Pressure (P)**
 The force exerted by the gas particles per unit area on the walls of the container.
 
 

 **Volume (V)**
 The space occupied by the gas.
 
 

 **Temperature (T)**
 A measure of the average kinetic energy of the gas particles.
 
 

 **Boltzmann Constant (k)**
 A physical constant relating the average kinetic energy of particles in a gas with the temperature of the gas.
 
 

 **Ideal Gas Law**
 PV = nRT, where n is the number of moles and R is the universal gas constant.

questions.question: Which of the following is a possible criticism of privatisation?

options.text: Expansion of bureaucracy and efficiency in public enterprises
Excessive government interference into private businesses
Limited access to essential services for marginalised populations
Reduced competition and innovation in the market

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Limited access to essential services for marginalised populations**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Equity Issues**: Privatisation can lead to inequitable access to essential services, as private entities may prioritize profit over service provision to marginalized groups.
 
• **Service Costs**: Private companies may increase the cost of services, making them less affordable for low-income populations.
 
• **Quality of Service**: There is a risk that private companies may cut corners in service quality to maximize profits.
 
• **Accountability**: Public accountability might decrease, as private companies are not subject to the same level of scrutiny as public entities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Aspect
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Privatisation**
 The transfer of ownership, property, or business from the government to the private sector.
 
 

 **Public Services**
 Services provided by the government to its citizens, either directly or through financing private provision of services.
 
 

 **Market Efficiency**
 The extent to which market prices reflect all available, relevant information.
 
 

 **Profit Motive**
 The intent to achieve monetary gain in a transaction or material endeavor.
 
 

 **Regulation**
 Rules or directives made and maintained by an authority to regulate private sector activities.

questions.question: What are the elements in group zero commonly known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Inert gases**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Group 0** elements are located at the far right of the periodic table.
 
• These elements are also known as **noble gases** due to their lack of reactivity under most conditions.
 
• They have a **complete valence shell** of electrons, making them very stable and unlikely to participate in chemical reactions.
 
• The group includes **Helium (He), Neon (Ne), Argon (Ar), Krypton (Kr), Xenon (Xe),** and **Radon (Rn)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Helium (He)** has the lowest boiling and melting points among the elements, making it useful in cryogenics and as a cooling medium for nuclear reactors.
 
• **Neon (Ne)** is widely used in advertising signs due to its ability to emit bright light when electrified.
 
• **Argon (Ar)** is commonly used in welding and in incandescent light bulbs to prevent the tungsten filament from oxidizing.
 
• **Krypton (Kr)** and **Xenon (Xe)** are used in lighting and photography. Xenon is also used in ion propulsion systems for spacecraft.
 
• **Radon (Rn)**, being radioactive, poses health risks and is a concern in homes as it can accumulate in basements.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

 
 

 
 
List - I (Acid)

 
 
 
List - II (Food Source)

 
 
 

 
 
A.

 
 
 
Carbonic acid

 
 
 
1.

 
 
 
Mustard oil

 
 
 

 
 
B.

 
 
 
Lauric acid

 
 
 
2.

 
 
 
Butter

 
 
 

 
 
C.

 
 
 
Butyric acid

 
 
 
3.

 
 
 
Soda Water

 
 
 

 
 
D.

 
 
 
Erucic acid

 
 
 
4.

 
 
 
Coconut milk
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A - 3, B - 4, C - 2, D - 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carbonic acid**

 
 
• Carbonic acid is a chemical compound with the chemical formula H2CO3 (equivalently OC(OH)2).
 
• It is also a name sometimes given to solutions of carbon dioxide in water (carbonated water) because such solutions contain small amounts of H2CO3.
 
• In physiology, carbonic acid is described as volatile acid or respiratory acid, because it is the only acid excreted as a gas by the lungs.
 
 

 
• Lauric acid

 
 
• It ​is a saturated medium-chain fatty acid with a 12-carbon backbone.
 
• It is found in many vegetable fats and in coconut and palm kernel oils.
 
• It is a solid at room temperature but melts easily in boiling water, so liquid lauric acid can be treated with various solutes and used to determine their molecular masses.
 
 
 
• Butyric acid:
 
 
• Butyric acid is a colourless liquid.
 
• It is soluble in ethanol, water, and ether.
 
• Butyric acid is found in rancid butter.
 
• It is also found in milk and parmesan cheese.
 
• Butyric acid is used to make esters.
 
• It is also used as a fishing bait additive.
 
 

Thus, butyric acid is found in butter.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4bfe34083e8c541504e22d7e62c4561cb1063841074b3f83ceea505f4b2aa72b.png] 

 
• **Erucic acid**

 
 
• Mustard oil contains Erucic Acid, which is a monounsaturated omega-9 fatty acid.
 
• Erucic Acid is also found in rapeseed oil and is used in the production of industrial lubricants and in the manufacture of biodiesel.

questions.question:
Identify the INCORRECTLY matched pair(s) of the British Governor-Generals of India and the events with which they are associated.

(i) Lord Dalhousie - Revolt of 1857

(ii) Lord Auckland - First Afghan War

(iii) Lord Canning - Wood's Despatch 1854
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Only (i) and (iii__)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Revolt of 1857**

 
 
• The Revolt of 1857 was the first rebellion against the British East India Company.
 
• The first war of Indian Independence started on 10th May 1857.
 
• The revolt was started at Meerut.
 
• It began as a revolt of the sepoys of the British East India Company’s army but eventually secured the participation of the masses.
 
• The issue of greased cartridges and military grievances has been over-emphasized as the factor for the Revolt of 1857.
 
• In March 1857, Mangal Pandey, a sepoy in Barrackpore, refused to use the cartridge and attacked his senior officers.
 
• He was hanged to death on 8th April 1857.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Afghan War**

 
 
• The Anglo-Afghan Wars were wars in which Great Britain, from its base in India, sought to extend its control over neighbouring Afghanistan and to oppose Russian influence there.
 
• There had been three Anglo-Afghan wars. The first, second and the third Anglo Afghan War taking place respectively in (1839–42), (1878–80) and (1919).
 
• The British, feeling that the then ruler of Afghanistan, DōstMoḥammad was either hostile to them or unable to resist the Russian penetration, moved to take a direct role in Afghan affairs. 
 
• The then Governor-general of India, Lord Auckland ordered an invasion of Afghanistan.
 
 
 
• Wood's Despatch:
 
 
• In 1854, Charles Wood prepared a Despatch on an educational system for India. It was considered the "Magna Carta of English Education in India".
 
• This document was the first comprehensive plan for the spread of education in India.

questions.question: Among the following diseases, which one is NOT inherited?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Malaria**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Down syndrome**, **Cystic fibrosis**, and **Muscular dystrophy** are genetic disorders passed from parents to children through genes.
 
• **Malaria** is caused by the Plasmodium parasites, which are transmitted to people through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
 
• Genetic disorders are inherited and are part of an individual's genetic makeup, whereas malaria is an infectious disease not determined by genetics.
 
• Understanding the difference between genetic and infectious diseases is crucial for diagnosis, treatment, and prevention strategies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Disease Type
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Genetic Disorders**
 Conditions caused by abnormalities in genes or chromosomes. Some may be inherited, while others occur due to mutations or changes in genes.
 
 

 **Infectious Diseases**
 Diseases caused by pathogenic microorganisms, such as bacteria, viruses, parasites, or fungi; can be spread, directly or indirectly, from one person to another.
 
 

 **Malaria**
 An infectious disease caused by Plasmodium parasites, transmitted to humans through the bite of infected Anopheles mosquitoes.
